notes: §1985:IX.4.9.3 SR3: "The INVALID KEY phrase must be specified if an applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure is not specified for the associated file-name". The 1985 text defines neither "applicable" nor "appropriate", and two final adjudications read it opposite ways (2026-11-12, kb/Work PB5413 amendment 1: reading A, a mode procedure is applicable to a statement of any file that can be open in that mode; 2026-11-14, op-20261114/held-adjudicated.json q1: reading B, only a mode in which the statement's condition can arise). So it is implementor latitude, and WiseOwl COBOL takes reading A as a DOCUMENTED LATITUDE CHOICE (kb/Work PB5591; docs/CONFORMANCE.md 3.5; docs/FILES_DESIGN.md D31(a)): reading B would refuse CCVS-85 SQ148A, GnuCOBOL 3.2 -std=cobol85 enforces none of the mandatory-phrase rules and so does not decide, and rejecting legal source is the worse harm. ExceptionPhraseRequirement.HasApplicableUse implements it: a declarative naming the file, or one for an open mode the file can be open in (EXTEND only for a file that can be opened EXTEND, kb/Work PB5413), refuses COBOL6826 otherwise. The witness (pb5591_indexed_input_use_excuses_write_85) runs at --std 85: the statement with no phrase is accepted under the one mode declarative, and at run time the procedure takes the logic-error status the statement raises in that mode (47, 48 or 49), matching the expectation derived from the text. The adjudication's probe (refute-rs-06/p/s-wr-ran-input.cob (ON INPUT only)) observed: compiles with no diagnostic: OPEN 00 / AFTER 22; exit 0, no procedure ran; under reading A that is the conforming result. Previous verdict: PARTIAL, held on reading B. Recorded 2026-11-14 by records-85-held from the final held-row adjudication (op-20261114/held-adjudicated.json).

next.reason: §1985:IX.4.9.3 SR3: 'The INVALID KEY phrase must be specified if an applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure is not specified for the associated file-name' (WRITE to an indexed file). 2023 has no such syntax rule (§2023:14.9.51.3) and states the refused case: §2023:9.1.14 GR4: 'If the INVALID KEY phrase is not specified in the input-output statement and there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement'; so too §2023:9.1.14 GR3: 'If control is returned from those statements or there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement'. The WRITE statement's general rules have no rule naming the phrases optional (DELETE, REWRITE and START each have one), so 'to' holds the two §2023:9.1.14 rules alone. Words that differ: 1985 'must be specified'; 2023 'not specified ... there are no applicable ... exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end'. A statement 1985 refuses is accepted by 2023 with a stated run-time effect: a lifted refusal, so CHANGED (kb/Work PB5021), not REMOVED.
